title: Polynomial-Time Unitary Synthesis from a Boolean Oracle
main_claim: For each n, a polynomial-time generator outputs one oracle circuit A_n over H, T, T†, CNOT with poly(n) qubits, gates, queries and query length. For every U in U(2^n) there is a Boolean f such that the channel of A_n^{O_f} is within 1/2 of U in full (unnormalized) diamond norm. The circuit depends only on n; f depends on U. This answers the constant-error Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis question positively.
coverage:
I read all seven sections and checked each step of the main chain.
(1) Lemma 3.1, the matrix sign estimate: Gaussian integration by parts, the weighted AM-GM step giving Tr(L X^l L X^{m-l}) ≤ Tr(L^2 X^m), the iteration, and the Rademacher comparison with 1/μ < 2.
(2) Prop 3.2: D = W* E1 M0 E2 W; the subgaussian tail bound and union bound 4qs·e^{-4(n+1)} < 1; v = 16s(n+1)/q; the dilation blocks; (2s)^{1/(2n+2)} ≤ √2; and E||D|| ≤ 16(n+1)√(s/q) ≤ 1/4 given M = 4096(n+1)^2. Also the s=1 case and the depth bound J.
(3) Lemma 4.1: VE = O, the norm identity giving F*F = I, and the formula for Y.
(4) Prop 4.2: tail bounds, the ω-averaging that separates degrees, CC* = I − DD* and B*B = I − D*D, the telescoping sum, and the intertwining bound 2τ.
(5) Prop 4.3: power-sum vectors with coordinates < 2^b recover the multiset via Newton's identities; the rightmost Z factor acts on input i; port inputs appear only at frequency 0.
(6) Lemma 5.1: the block ⟨j|B|ι⟩ = t0·T, orthogonality of the e'_j, the invariant planes, rotation by 2β per round, and the error (π+1)(1−σ) ≤ 5ε.
(7) Prop 5.2: the Fourier transforms commute with the embedding j.
(8) Lemma 6.1: the error chain, then multiplication by U_R*.
(9) Prop 6.2: r^L ≤ 3/L, total error 54/10000, and the resource exponents N^10 and N^13.
(10) Section 7: the trace 1+√2/2 is not an algebraic integer, so the rotation is irrational; the closure is a group; the commutator refinement gives error Cε^{3/2} with length 5ℓ; the phase-retaining compilation W = e^{iγ}S, with a scratch qubit carrying diag(e^{iγ}, e^{-iγ}); the telescoping composition of slot errors; and the final trace-norm bound 1/5.
Numerical checks: D0·Z·D0† = H, the parity identity for 4abc, and Tr V. I also ran a brute-force instance (k=2, s=2, L=2, n=2, |G| = 64^3). It confirmed that F is unitary, the Gram eigenvalues lie in [1 − r^{2L}, 1], the intertwining error is within 2τ, and every Fourier row of both field maps has at most L nonzero entries.
Not independently verified: the cited standard facts (QFT slot construction, multiplexor state preparation), beyond a sanity read.
